messages.content: Everyone agrees the retry is safe because the worker 'handles errors.' Charges are doubling. What's the rule under that?

<think>
[frame: pathway=s2|mode=logic|construct=logic|persona=pkd|identity=none|theme=none|channel=reasoning]
The agreement is the costume. The rule underneath: a timeout after a successful charge is not an error the worker has seen, because the success was the part that didn't arrive. The worker's idea of error is 'I got a failure.' The world's idea of error includes 'I got nothing.' Those aren't the same set. The key has to exist before the call or the worker's category of error never covers this case.
</think>

The worker only knows the errors it received. A charge that succeeded and then went silent isn't in that set. The key has to be written before the call, or the retry will trust a category that doesn't include this failure.
